parts.name: base grip

physics.Basic_description: Dark grey curved plastic handle forming the bottom base of the stapler with a matte finish.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the structural foundation and lower grip surface for the user's hand to press against.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper would clamp onto the curved body of the base to stabilize the object during operation.
physics.reason: Injection molded plastic housing typically has thin walls to save weight and material, enclosing an empty cavity or internal frame.

parts.description: Dark grey curved plastic handle forming the bottom base of the stapler with a matte finish.

parts.name: grip ridge 0

physics.Basic_description: Small green textured pads embedded along the side of the dark grey base handle.
physics.Functional_description: Increases friction and comfort for the user's fingers to prevent slipping during use.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and flush to be grasped individually; they serve as contact points for a grip on the base.
physics.reason: These are small overmolded or inserted rubber pads that are solid throughout their small volume.

parts.name: anvil plate

physics.Basic_description: Small rectangular metallic plate with two slots located at the front tip of the base.
physics.Functional_description: Receives the staple legs and bends them inward to secure the paper.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a grasp target; too small and located at the functional tip where obstruction would occur.
physics.reason: Must be solid metal to withstand the impact force of staples without deforming.

parts.description: Small rectangular metallic plate with two slots located at the front tip of the base.

parts.name: hinge knuckles

physics.Basic_description: Yellowish-grey blocky plastic components at the rear connecting the top arm to the base.
physics.Functional_description: Houses the pivot mechanism allowing the top arm to rotate relative to the base.
physics.Grasped_description: Not suitable for grasping due to small size and location at the joint mechanism.
physics.reason: Structural hinge components in small tools are typically solid or thick-walled to handle shear forces.

parts.description: Yellowish-grey blocky plastic components at the rear connecting the top arm to the base.
parts.function: Houses the pivot mechanism allowing the top arm to rotate relative to the base.

parts.name: torsion spring

physics.Basic_description: Coiled metal wire spring visible within the hinge assembly at the rear.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the restoring force to return the top arm to the open position after stapling.
physics.Grasped_description: Internal component, not accessible or suitable for grasping.
physics.reason: Springs are made of solid wire wound into a coil.

parts.description: Coiled metal wire spring visible within the hinge assembly at the rear.
parts.function: Provides the restoring force to return the top arm to the open position after stapling.

parts.name: arm shell

physics.Basic_description: Large white elongated plastic cover forming the upper body of the stapler with a smooth matte finish.
physics.Functional_description: Encloses the internal stapling mechanism and provides the upper surface for the user to press down.
physics.Grasped_description: Primary grasp target for the top jaw; a gripper would press down on this surface to actuate the stapler.
physics.reason: This is a cosmetic and protective shell covering the internal metal rail and spring mechanism, definitely not a solid block of plastic.

parts.description: Large white elongated plastic cover forming the upper body of the stapler with a smooth matte finish.
parts.function: Encloses the internal stapling mechanism and provides the upper surface for the user to press down.

parts.name: carrier rail

physics.Basic_description: Cyan-colored metal channel visible inside the white arm shell near the hinge.
physics.Functional_description: Guides the strip of staples and supports the driver blade mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: Internal component, generally obscured by the shell and not a grasp target.
physics.reason: Stamped sheet metal channel used for guiding staples is a thin-walled structure.

parts.description: Cyan-colored metal channel visible inside the white arm shell near the hinge.

parts.name: driver blade

physics.Basic_description: Small magenta-colored metal tip located at the front end of the internal mechanism.
physics.Functional_description: Pushes the staple out of the carrier and through the paper when the arm is pressed.
physics.Grasped_description: Tiny functional tip, not graspable.
physics.reason: Must be a solid piece of hardened metal to transfer force without buckling.

parts.description: Small magenta-colored metal tip located at the front end of the internal mechanism.
parts.function: Pushes the staple out of the carrier and through the paper when the arm is pressed.

parts.name: hinge pin

physics.Basic_description: Small pink cylindrical pin located at the center of the hinge assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as the axle for the rotation between the top arm and the base.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and recessed to be grasped.
physics.reason: Pins are solid cylinders to resist shear forces.

parts.description: Small pink cylindrical pin located at the center of the hinge assembly.
parts.function: Acts as the axle for the rotation between the top arm and the base.

parts.name: grip rib 0

physics.Basic_description: Series of lime-green raised ridges running along the top surface of the white arm shell.
physics.Functional_description: Provides tactile feedback and prevents the user's thumb from slipping when pressing down.
physics.Grasped_description: Part of the top surface texture; a gripper would contact these when grasping the arm shell.
physics.reason: These are likely molded features integral to the shell or small solid inserts, effectively solid in the context of grasp physics.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
